events.content:
I want a small app for keeping track of the books I'm reading.

When I open it I want to see what I'm currently reading and what I've finished. I want to add a book from a form, mark one as finished, and click through to a book to see its title, author and my notes. I'd like to be able to send someone a link to a single book.

Nothing fancy and no accounts. Skip the database, save the books to a JSON file so they're still there after a restart.

events.content:
Done. The app is a single zero-dependency Node server, `server.mjs` — run it with `npm start` and open http://localhost:3000 (set `PORT` to change it).

What you get:

- **Home page** shows two sections, Currently reading and Finished, plus an "Add a book" form with title, author, and optional notes.
- **Each book links to its own page** at `/book/<id>` showing title, author, status, and your notes — that URL is stable and shareable, so you can send it to someone directly.
- **"Finished it" button** appears next to unfinished books on the list and on the book page; clicking it moves the book to Finished (and records when).
- **Storage** is a plain `books.json` next to the server, written atomically (write-to-temp-then-rename) so a crash mid-save can't corrupt it. I added it to `.gitignore` since it's your personal data.

I verified the whole flow with curl: added two books, viewed the detail page with multi-line notes, marked one finished (it redirects back to wherever you clicked from), confirmed 404 for unknown ids and a 400 when title/author are missing, then restarted the server and confirmed both books were still there. Test data was removed afterward, so you start with a clean slate.

Small details worth knowing: everything is server-rendered HTML with no JavaScript on the page, all user text is HTML-escaped, and the styling respects light/dark mode. If you later want editing notes or "want to read" as a third status, both would be small additions.
